articles.title: Tata Motors raises Iveco takeover offer price to 14.40 euro per share
No higher bid: Tata Motors’ final price faces crucial test as Iveco shareholders hold the key
Stellantis and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles broaden partnership to develop vehicles in Pune
Tata Motors, Stellantis expand partnership: New deal details explained
Tata Motors sweetens Iveco offer as key investors hold out

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors increased its all‑cash voluntary tender offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the deal at €3.91 billion (a 33.47% premium to the July 17 2025 price and 6.77% to the July 29 2025 price). The offer, described as final, will be funded partly by an €85 million credit facility with MUFG Bank. The acceptance period runs from 7 September to 26 October 2026, with an extraordinary general meeting set for 16 October 2026.

Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion bid for Iveco is at its “best and final” price of €14.40 per share. The outcome now hinges on whether shareholders will tender enough shares to meet either the original 95% threshold or a lower 80% threshold, with Exor’s 27.06% stake (43% voting rights) already pledged. Analysts note that a failed deal would hurt Iveco more than Tata Motors, while completion would create a global commercial‑vehicle group with about €21 billion revenue and 5,90,000 vehicles annually.

Stellantis India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and its subsidiary signed a definitive agreement expanding their partnership into advanced vehicle technology and product collaboration. Under the deal Tata will provide Stellantis access to its product technology and architecture, with vehicles to be built in India at the 50:50 FIAPL joint venture, targeting more than 50 global markets.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis have formalised an expanded partnership that combines Tata’s vehicle architecture and technology with Stellantis’ global product‑development expertise. The agreement, announced on 12 October 2026, builds on a February 2026 MoU and will see vehicles developed for over 50 markets being manufactured in India at the FIAPL joint venture.

Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share (a 2% increase) after activist Petrus Advisers rejected the earlier price. The revised price is described as the best and final offer. Yet three major shareholders—Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers—holding about 20.4% of Iveco’s shares have not tendered, leaving acceptance at only 28.4% as the 26 October deadline approaches. Exor has pledged its 27.06% stake and holds 43% of voting rights.

key_points.text: Tata Motors raised its takeover offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at €3.91 billion, a 33.47% premium over the July 17 2025 price and a 6.77% premium over the July 29 2025 price.
The revised offer is Tata Motors’ “best and final” price and will not be increased further.
Tata Motors will fund the additional payout with an €85 million credit facility from MUFG Bank Ltd.
The tender offer runs from 7 September to 26 October 2026, with an extraordinary general meeting scheduled for 16 October 2026.
Acceptances have covered only 28.4% of Iveco shares, putting the acquisition at risk ahead of the 26 October deadline.
Exor, Iveco’s largest shareholder, has pledged its 27.06% stake (holding 43% of voting rights) and supports the transaction.
If completed, the combined entity would generate roughly €21 billion of annual revenue and sell about 5,90,000 vehicles per year.

Tata Motors and Stellantis have signed a definitive agreement expanding their partnership to co‑develop vehicles using Tata’s product technology and architecture, with manufacturing in India at the 50:50 FIAPL joint venture, targeting more than 50 global markets.
The partnership builds on a February 2026 MoU and aims to leverage India’s engineering expertise for export‑focused vehicle programmes.

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors must convince silent shareholders, who own about 27% of Iveco’s common shares, to reach the 80% acceptance needed for its €3.9 billion acquisition. About 52.9% of shares voted in favour, while non‑promoter opposition voted against board appointments. The offer price was sweetened to €14.40 per share.

Analysts preview Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27, expecting volume growth around 43% YoY, revenue up 44‑45% YoY to roughly Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore, and PAT growth of 44.3% (JM) or 25.7% (MOFSL). Margin direction is disputed, with differing views on EBITDA trends.

Tata Motors overtook Mahindra to become India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle maker in April‑Sept FY27, posting a 43% rise in domestic dispatches to over 3.9 lakh units, helped by a 59% jump in utility‑vehicle dispatches. The overall passenger‑vehicle market grew 28.3% to about 26.4 lakh units.

Iveco Group shareholders approved all resolutions linked to Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion takeover, lowering the mandatory acceptance threshold from 95% to 80% and clearing a key hurdle for the transaction. The offer price stands at €14.40 per share, with the tender set to close on Oct 26 2026.

Iveco shareholders approved Tata Motors’ takeover bid, cutting the acceptance threshold to 80 % and confirming the €14.40 per share offer (previously €14.10). The tender runs Sep 7‑Oct 26 2026, valuing the deal at roughly €3.8 billion.

key_points.text: Tata Motors needs to secure 80% shareholder acceptance for the Iveco acquisition; silent shareholders holding ~27% of shares must be persuaded, with current supportive votes covering ~52.9% of common shares and opposition to board appointments evident; the offer price was increased to €14.40 per share.

Analysts forecast Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27 volume growth of about 43% YoY, revenue growth of 44‑45% YoY to Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore, and PAT growth of 44.3% (JM) or 25.7% (MOFSL), while margin outlook is split between expected improvement and decline.

Tata Motors became India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle manufacturer in April‑Sept FY27, with domestic passenger‑vehicle dispatches up 43% to over 3.9 lakh units and utility‑vehicle dispatches up 59%, overtaking Mahindra.

Iveco shareholders approved the takeover proposals, reducing the minimum acceptance threshold from 95% to 80% and authorising post‑offer demerger and delisting steps, clearing a key hurdle for Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion acquisition at €14.40 per share.

industry_context.text: The Indian passenger‑vehicle market recorded robust growth, with domestic dispatches increasing 28.3% to around 26.4 lakh units in April‑Sept FY27.

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors' €3.9 billion acquisition of Iveco faces a hurdle as silent shareholders—roughly three‑in‑four investors who did not vote—must be persuaded to reach the 80% acceptance needed for full control. About 52.9% of Iveco's common shares backed the deal, while opposition centers on board appointments. The offer was sweetened to €14.40 per share. If Tata crosses the 66.67% threshold but not 80%, it can waive the higher threshold but cannot delist Iveco. The combined business would generate about €21 billion in annual revenue and sell over 590,000 vehicles.

Analysts preview Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27 expecting volume growth of around 43% YoY to 1,35,114‑1,37,339 units, revenue up 44‑45% YoY to Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore, and adjusted PAT rising 25.7‑44.3% YoY. Margins are seen under pressure despite a 2.5% price hike, with divergent views on EBITDA margin trends. Light commercial vehicle volumes led the expansion, rising 53.1% YoY.

Three investors (Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital, Petrus Advisers) hold about 20.4% of Iveco and could gain roughly €63 million at the €14.40 per‑share offer, influencing the 80% threshold. As of 21 Oct, shareholders have tendered about 33.4% of Iveco shares; the offer closes on 26 Oct. Iveco’s defence business was sold to Leonardo for €1.7 billion, with dividends paid in April 2026. Tata's revised offer price is €14.40 per share.
Tata Motors is listed among several stocks that investors will watch on 23 Oct as they track September‑quarter earnings and other corporate updates.
Tata Motors reported Q2 FY27 consolidated profit of ₹1,257 crore with revenue rising 36.3% YoY. Shares fell about 4% ahead of the results, trading at ₹395.45.
